title: 4.6 beta 2 - Incorect material distance fade origin
body: # Tested versions - Godot 4.5 - Godot 4.6 beta 2 # System information **Godot v4.6.beta2 - Gentoo 2.18 on Tty - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB (nvidia; 580.95.05) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-2600 CPU @ 3.40GHz (8 threads) - 31.32 Gio memory** # Issue description ## A bit of context This issue is not directly related to [102799](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102799) but it would make sense to investigate the below to have consistent behaviors across LoD solutions proposed in documentation [here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/3d/visibility_ranges.html#use-dithering-for-lod-transitions) : Indeed, using dithering for LoD transition as shown in the documentation require to use `visibility range` along side `distance fade`. While the fix for [102799](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102799) is a great progress `distance fade` doesn't work yet (and probably never worked) with `MultiMeshInstance3D` since the origin computed for each process (`distance fade` and `visibility range`) doesn't seem to be the same. ## The real thing ### Material's distance fade only As shown below the blue `MultiMeshInstance3D` is getting more dithered as the camera is going further from the world origin (The red cube). On the contrary, getting close to the world origin bring the blue `MultiMeshInstance3D` visibility back. ### Visibility range only On the other side we have the green `MultiMeshInstance3D` which behave differently depending on which Godot version you use (`4.5` or `4.6 beta-2`) Here, we're looking at the expected result as fixed in upcoming Godot `4.6`. Indeed, going close to the center of the `MultiMeshInstance3D` make it visible. Unlike the case where the camera is getting close to the world origin : ## Expected Fix My understanding of the documentation would imply that the material's `fade distance` set of attributes should behave like the bug-fixed `visibility range`. This way we could effectively control what's should be on screen or not depending on the distance. ## User side work around Right now, it is impossible to combine both techniques for `MultiMeshInstance3D` effectively. This could be mitigated by manually changing the origin of the `MultiMeshInstance3D` or setting up a custom AABB (I did not test the later) but it introduce more code bloat and headache than some well defined behaviors in documentation and consistent fading techniques. # Steps to reproduce ## Generating a MultiMeshInstance3D Something like this will do ```gdscript func create_a_new_multimesh_instance3D(offset:Vector3,color:Color) -> MultiMeshInstance3D: var mii:MultiMeshInstance3D = MultiMeshInstance3D.new() var multimesh = MultiMesh.new() multimesh.mesh = BoxMesh.new() multimesh.transform_format = MultiMesh.TRANSFORM_3D multimesh.instance_count = 8 multimesh.visible_instance_count = 8 for i in range(0, 8): multimesh.set_instance_transform( i, Transform3D( Basis.IDENTITY, offset + Vector3( 0, 0, i*1.5 ) ) ) mii.multimesh = multimesh # colors setup for clarity var mat = StandardMaterial3D.new() mat.emission_enabled = true mat.emission = color mat.emission_energy_multiplier = 0.01 mat.albedo_color = color mii.multimesh.mesh.surface_set_material(0, mat) ``` then ## Setup the fading technique ```gdscript func _ready() -> void: var visible_range:MultiMeshInstance3D = create_a_new_multimesh_instance3D(Vector3(-8,0,0), Color.GREEN) visible_range.visibility_range_end = 8 visible_range.visibility_range_end_margin = 1 visible_range.visibility_range_fade_mode = MultiMeshInstance3D.VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_SELF var distance_fade:MultiMeshInstance3D = create_a_new_multimesh_instance3D(Vector3(8,0,0),Color.BLUE) distance_fade.multimesh.mesh.surface_get_material(0).distance_fade_mode = BaseMaterial3D.DISTANCE_FADE_OBJECT_DITHER distance_fade.multimesh.mesh.surface_get_material(0).distance_fade_min_distance = 8 distance_fade.multimesh.mesh.surface_get_material(0).distance_fade_max_distance = 1 var origin:MeshInstance3D = MeshInstance3D.new() origin.mesh = BoxMesh.new() var mat = StandardMaterial3D.new() mat.emission_enabled = true mat.emission = Color.RED mat.emission_energy_multiplier = 0.01 mat.albedo_color = Color.RED origin.set_surface_override_material(0, mat) add_child(visible_range) add_child(distance_fade) add_child(origin) ``` Both `MultiMeshinstance3D` have their origin set to world origin. # Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Here is a MRP which include the above code so you can test it yourself. [BrokenDistanceFade_MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24401706/BrokenDistanceFade_MRP.zip)
